ast-grep.note: In-repo copy carries THREE adaptations; re-apply all three after any re-vendor from upstream, then --relock. (1) A documentation-style split of one 41-word sentence into three, per .claude/rules/documentation-style.md. (2) `Bash(sg:*)` REMOVED from allowed-tools, 2026-09-02. Upstream ships `sg` as ast-grep's short alias, but on Ubuntu /usr/bin/sg is a different program from the login package that runs a command under another group through /bin/sh. A skill grant is a grant and never a limit, so that line permitted `sg <group> -c "<any command>"`: a general command runner. Nothing in the skill or its two reference files ever invoked `sg`. Do not restore it on a re-vendor. (3) A Step 0 binary preflight, because the skill is router: auto while ast-grep may be absent, and `command -v sg` resolves to the wrong program.
